$comment: Rotating draft briefs per brand — the seed lane's content plan. `node scripts/social-drafts.mjs seed --auto` picks the week's briefs by ISO-week rotation and files them as SocialDraftRequest asks; the 5-minute drain answers them on the Max pool, and the copy lands in the Hub for a human to stage. Briefs follow the /draft contract: the fact, the audience, the CTA, the hard constraints — plus Angle (which of the three angles this brief is pre-committed to), The scene (a moment the audience owns, so the writer opens on something that is not a feature), and Register (the rung from content/docs/social/copy.mdx). All of it goes INSIDE the brief string: the calendar panel and the seeder both read only `brief`, so a new JSON field would be written and read by nobody — which is exactly what happened to `pillar`. Never a metric, customer, price, or date that isn't true — the drafting session will refuse to invent one. Edit freely; rotation is stateless (ISO week % length), so order is cadence. Pillars per brand: content/docs/social/<brand>.mdx. | `visual` names the raster asset a post wants from the seat lane (null = the template lane owns its image).

hogwarts.brief: Feature highlight: online admission — parents apply from their phone, the school tracks every application on one dashboard instead of paper folders. Audience: school owners and administrators in MENA. CTA: book a demo at https://ed.databayt.org. Suggested visual: admission dashboard card (template lane, og type). Constraint: no invented numbers — the promise is 'the paper chase ends', not a percentage. Angle: the admissions office gets its people back. The scene: first week of the season — a queue at the door, paper files on the desk, a phone that does not stop. Register: rung 2.

visual.subject: A school front office counter, clean and unhurried, no queue, quiet wall behind it

hogwarts.brief: Feature highlight: attendance in one tap — the teacher marks the class in seconds and a parent sees it the same moment. Audience: teachers first, parents second. CTA: see it live at https://ed.databayt.org. Suggested visual: classroom lifestyle photo (library: hw-classroom). Constraint: truthful — instant visibility is the feature, don't promise SMS/WhatsApp delivery. Angle: the first two minutes of every period, given back. The scene: the register going down the row while the lesson waits, and a name called twice because the sheet was already passed. Register: rung 2.

visual.subject: A teacher at the front of a class holding a tablet, mid-motion marking the register, students blurred at their desks

hogwarts.brief: Administrator time-savings: invoices and receipts come out of the system, not out of a spreadsheet — fees, installments, and who-paid-what in one view. Audience: school owners. CTA: https://ed.databayt.org. Suggested visual: og card with one strong Arabic line. Constraint: no claimed hours-saved figure; 'the end-of-term spreadsheet night' is the pain to name. Angle: the night the books are reconciled by hand. The scene: a ledger open beside a laptop, the same number typed into both, and a total that refuses to agree with itself. Register: rung 2.

visual.subject: A school bursar’s desk — closed ledger books stacked to one side, an open laptop beside them, warm afternoon light

hogwarts.brief: MENA education context: hogwarts is Arabic-first and RTL-native — built in Arabic, not translated into it. Menus, report cards, parent messages: all native. Audience: everyone; administrators decide, parents trust. CTA: https://ed.databayt.org. Suggested visual: split card (template lane) — Arabic UI beside English UI. Constraint: keep it proud but calm, no competitor-bashing. Angle: built in Arabic, not translated into it — and a parent can feel the difference in one screen. The scene: the report card that reads right to left with no English label stranded in a corner, and no date written backwards. Register: rung 2.

Feature highlight: the timetable builder catches conflicts before the term starts — a teacher can't be in two rooms, a room can't hold two classes. Audience: administrators who build the schedule every term. CTA: book a demo at https://ed.databayt.org. Suggested visual: og card. Constraint: the feature is conflict detection at build time — nothing about AI optimization. Angle: the clash is found in the week before term, not in the first period of it. The scene: a printed timetable on the wall with three cells circled in red, and a teacher who is somehow in two rooms at nine o'clock. Register: rung 2.

Open-source trust: hogwarts is open source — a school can read exactly how its students' data is handled, and its IT can self-host if policy requires. Audience: school owners and IT decision-makers. CTA: the code and a demo at https://ed.databayt.org. Suggested visual: og card with the repo motif. Constraint: true today — open source on GitHub; don't promise certifications we don't hold. Angle: you can read the code that holds your students' records. The scene: the question that stops a procurement meeting — where does this data actually live, and who else can see it? Register: rung 2. Say the guarantee in the reader's words, never the engineer's — 'your school's records stay your school's', not tenant scoping or reads and writes.

Parent visibility: one place where a parent sees attendance, grades, and fees for every child they have in the school. Audience: parents (the B2C trust that closes the B2B sale). CTA: ask your school about hogwarts — https://ed.databayt.org. Suggested visual: lifestyle photo (library: hw-dashboard-device). Constraint: calm reassurance, not surveillance framing. Angle: three children in the school should not mean three people to ask. The scene: a parent at the gate at pick-up, phone in hand, finding the answer before the teacher reaches the door. Register: rung 2, warmed — the reader is a parent, so second person is allowed.

visual.subject: A parent's hands holding a phone in a school corridor, other parents soft in the background

hogwarts.brief: Feature highlight: exams and grades — marks entered once become report cards, transcripts, and the parent's view without re-typing. Audience: teachers and administrators at term end. CTA: https://ed.databayt.org. Suggested visual: og card. Constraint: the claim is single entry, many outputs — no 'auto-grading' language. Angle: one entry, many outputs. The scene: end of term — marks entered, then copied, then typed again, and every copy is another chance for an error. Register: rung 2. Note: this brief already has a shipped sibling in the carousel lane (hogwarts/carousels/exams-one-entry.json); write a different opening, do not reuse its first line.

visual.subject: A squared stack of paper report cards on a desk next to a closed laptop, raking daylight

balqalam.brief: Feature highlight: one system instead of five notebooks and a WhatsApp group — admission, attendance, grades, timetable, exams and fees in a single place, addressed to Arabic-speaking schools. Audience: school owners and principals in Saudi Arabia and the wider Arabic MENA market; administrators, not technologists. CTA: احجز عرضاً at https://balqalam.com. Suggested visual: an unhurried principal's desk (plate). Constraint: no invented numbers and no percentages — the promise is that the school stops living in separate notebooks, not a measured saving. Never carry the Hogwarts wordmark on a balqalam asset. Angle: the argument is competence, not enthusiasm. The scene: the end of a working day, one laptop open, the paper stacks gone. Register: rung 2.

Audience: teachers and heads of department in Arabic-speaking schools. CTA: جرّبها at https://balqalam.com. Suggested visual: a single clean grade column on a tablet (product). The scene: a tablet on a staffroom table, one column filled, no duplicate paperwork beside it. Register: rung 2.

balqalam.brief: Context: the Gulf school year starts in late August, and the schools that begin it calmly are the ones that set up before the first bell rather than during the first week. Audience: Saudi and Gulf school owners deciding now, in the weeks before term. CTA: ابدأ قبل الجرس at https://balqalam.com. Suggested visual: template lane — an Arabic type card, no photograph. Constraint: no urgency manufactured beyond the real calendar, no countdown pressure, no invented enrolment numbers. Never carry the Hogwarts wordmark. Angle: readiness is quieter than rescue. The scene: none — this one is typographic. Register: rung 2.

databayt.brief: The company story: databayt builds its software in the open — the repositories are public, the issues are public, and the work is readable while it happens rather than after it ships. Audience: developers, contributors and the Arabic-speaking MENA tech community; technical readers who want detail, not slogans. CTA: read the code at https://github.com/databayt. Suggested visual: template lane — a typographic card, no photograph. Constraint: describe only what is genuinely public; do not overstate the size of the team or the community, and do not claim adoption we cannot show. The Sudan clause binds: humility in tone, never trade on crisis. Constraint: databayt has no mark file — the wordmark carries the asset and the corner stays quiet. Angle: building in public is a working method, not a marketing posture. Register: rung 2.

The doctrine: a contributor revenue-share model — people who build the software share in what it earns, across three business models (Per Project, Partners, Codebase). Audience: contributors, partners and talent weighing whether to work with a small open-source company. CTA: see how it works at https://databayt.org. Suggested visual: template lane — Arabic type card. Constraint: describe the model as it is actually written; quote no earnings figures and promise no income. The Sudan clause binds: humility, never crisis-as-hook. databayt has no mark file — wordmark only, corner quiet. Angle: the sharing economy is the company's structure, not a slogan bolted onto it. Register: rung 2.

How the work is done: a small team runs a software company with Claude Code — configuration over construction, guardrails written down, and the same engine driving the technical and the business side. Audience: developers and technical founders curious about the practice, not the product. CTA: read the engine at https://kun.databayt.org. Suggested visual: one laptop, terminal open (mockup). Constraint: no productivity multiplier claims and no invented output figures — describe the method, not a speedup. AI-disclosure attaches to the IMAGE, not the text — it is the piece's aiGenerated flag and the platform's own label. Never write a bracketed stage direction such as [Visual: …] or [صورة: …] into the post copy; the copy is what publishes. databayt has no mark file — leave the corner quiet. Angle: the interesting part is the configuration, not the autocomplete. The scene: a plain desk, a single laptop with a terminal session, no faces and no branding on the machine. Register: rung 3 — this one may be written in English where the subject is deep-technical.

visual.subject: A single laptop on a plain desk with a terminal session open, no faces, no branding visible on the machine

The Sudan clause binds: humility in tone, never exploit hardship for engagement. databayt has no mark file — wordmark only, corner quiet. Angle: the boring work is the expensive work. The scene: an empty desk at first light, one monitor showing a completed run, a quiet wall behind it. Register: rung 2.
